svg.title: Anatomy of a QR code
svg.desc: A labelled QR code showing the finder patterns, timing patterns, alignment pattern, format information, data and error correction area, quiet zone, and the empty corner that shows orientation.
svg.text: Anatomy of a QR code
Example: a version 2 code (25 × 25 modules) for https://qrhere.online/
Finder patterns
Three big squares. Scanners look for these first
to find the code and its direction.
Timing patterns
Alternating dark and light dots. Counting them
tells the scanner how big each module is.
Alignment pattern
A smaller square that helps correct tilt and
bending. Bigger codes have more of them.
Format information
Stores the error correction level and the mask
pattern used. It is written in two places.
Data and error correction
The message itself, plus backup data used to
repair smudged or damaged modules.
Quiet zone
A blank margin, at least 4 modules wide, so the
code is not confused with what is around it.
The empty corner
Only three corners have a finder square. The
missing one shows the scanner which way is up.
Quiet zone: 4 modules of blank space on every side
qrhere.online
